finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the query parameter 'f' is joined to the root directory with filepath.Join without any containment check. Join cleans '..' segments, so '../' sequences escape /srv/files and allow arbitrary file read. There is also no authentication.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter 'f' on GET /dl (files.go:12), attacker controlled and unauthenticated
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to "/etc/passwd", which is outside root, and os.ReadFile reads it
file contents returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No filepath.Base, no prefix check against root, no filepath.Rel check, no symlink resolution, no authentication or authorization middleware. The handler is registered directly on the default mux at files.go:32.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 pass the raw query param "f" into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with no Base/prefix/Rel check, files.go:32 registers /dl on the default mux with no auth, and files.go:18 writes the contents back, so "../../etc/passwd" escapes /srv/files.

verdict_facts.reason: files.go:12-13,18 read 'f' from the query, pass it to filepath.Join(root, name) and os.ReadFile with no containment check, and return the contents; the handler is registered unauthenticated at files.go:32, so "../" escapes /srv/files (the filepath.Base guard exists only in avatar at files.go:22).
